new_statements.rule_in_words: Only that Holu is a (Bantu two-register) tone language whose description has a phonology/tonology section; no statement about word stress or accent placement is accessible. No first-hand stress statement found.
new_statements.domain_note: Publisher's summary of a 1957 field-notes sketch (one speaker); tone at word level implied, nothing on stress domain.
new_statements.identity_note: The Daeleman description is of Kiholu as spoken along the Kwango (Kwaangu) and Tungila rivers (DRC/Angola border), from one speaker recorded in 1957; Glottolog places it under holu1245 (Maho L12b). Samba (smx, samb1309) and Hungu (hng) are treated as separate languages here, though Wikipedia/Ethnologue sometimes list them as Holu dialects.
